specification_purpose: Authorize exactly one bounded v6 selection grid run over the frozen v6 candidate set, under the unchanged v1 selection rule, on development data only, writing only to the v6 paths, with the effective v6 rules and the v6-cutoff-bounded benchmark built in. This artifact names the execution path, the bounds, the benchmark rule, the stopping conditions, the rollback rule and the falsifiers of that run. Building it executes nothing: no grid is run, no candle is read, no result exists. The v6 execution path src/v6_campaign does not exist yet; the authorization records v6_execution_path_exists: false and binds no path digest.

prerequisites_delivered: the v6 candidate manifest freeze configs/research_v6_candidate_freeze.json
design_basis.execution_path_outside_hashed_set: The v6 execution code will live in src/v6_campaign, outside the hashed source set src/breakout_research. The path does not exist yet, so no path digest is bound. It will import the v1 engine unchanged; it adds, edits and removes no file under src/breakout_research, so the v1 campaign authorization and the identity tuples stay valid.

authorized_run.authorization_note: The run is recorded in the ledger before the first result is written. The authorization permits one logical run: a completed run is never re-run, and an interrupted run is resumed from the verified shards, with the number of resumes bounded by max_retries_on_technical_failure. A boundary abort rolls the ledger back and releases the run, so that a defect can be fixed and the run started again.

resume_semantics.note: A process that is killed leaves the run in the ledger as RUNNING. The next process resumes it from the verified shards instead of starting a second run, so an interruption cannot burn the single authorized run.

scope.membership_rule: Exactly the constituents marked validated in research/universe_manifest_v6.json. The run may not re-rank, widen or narrow the frozen set.

execution_path.note: The v6 execution path src/v6_campaign does not exist yet. When it is created, its canonical source digest will be recorded here and the path must live outside src/breakout_research. It reuses the v1 indicators, signals, backtester, verified candle loader, shard writer, checkpoint manager and candidate selector without modification. It adds no parameter, threshold, fold, cost or selection criterion of its own.

code_identity.algorithm_description: sha256 over the concatenation, for every *.py file under the root in ascending POSIX relative-path order, of the relative path, a newline, the sha256 hex digest of the file bytes, and a newline.
code_identity.note: The identity of a v6 run is the composite of the canonical digest of the hashed v1 engine and the canonical digest of the v6 execution path. Because the execution path does not exist yet, its digest is null and the run code identity is computed over a null execution path digest. The checkout-dependent ordered digest compute_code_hash() stays the authorized value of record and is never used as an identity.

membership.rule: a candle is inside a confirmatory window when its close falls strictly after that window's start and before its end, regardless of which asset the candle belongs to; a candle that closes exactly at a window's start is development data
membership.consequence_for_the_run: a candle that closes exactly at a confirmatory window's start is development data; the last development candle of every v6 dataset closes exactly at the effective development boundary

overlap.rule: the v6 evaluation may not start before the later of the four recorded confirmatory gates and the v6 window's own earliest end; the v6 confirmatory window opens inside the still-open v2, v3, v4 and v5 confirmatory windows in time, which is inevitable and not a violation: the v6 candidate set is disjoint from the v1, v2, v3, v4 and v5 candidate sets
overlap.consequence_for_the_run: the v6 confirmatory evaluation may not start before the effective gate; the v6 selection run itself reads development data only

execution.precedence: the effective v6 execution protocol is configs/research_v6_execution.json; v6 publishes no execution amendment; the protocol stays on disk, unchanged and visible
execution.named_amendment_precedence: no v6 execution amendment exists yet
execution.consequence_for_the_run: the effective execution protocol is the frozen protocol; the run gate verifies the published v6 selection authorization's identity instead of a static flag

data_boundary.candles_before_utc_rule: Only candles that close at or before the effective development boundary recorded by the candidate freeze may be read during the selection run. The effective boundary is the earlier of the v6 confirmatory-window start and the preregistered development cutoff, so no run can read a candle that closes inside the open v2, v3, v4 or v5 confirmatory window. A dataset that reaches past the boundary is refused before it is read.
data_boundary.boundary_convention: inclusive: the last development candle closes exactly at the boundary
data_boundary.development_cutoff_rule: configs/research_v6.json#holdout.development_cutoff_utc: the v6 development data ends at the last fully closed hour that closes at or before the cutoff, and no candle that closes after the cutoff may be read
data_boundary.provider_requests_note: The run reads the immutable local datasets that the effective v6 data manifest already binds and verifies, the benchmark dataset included. It performs no provider request, so it cannot re-retrieve, re-time or refresh any market data.

selection_rule.grid_reference: the strategy_grid of configs/research_v1.json, inherited unchanged by configs/research_v6.json: 2304 configurations per asset

bounds.planned_execution_units_note: The bounded run holds 7 assets x 2304 configurations x 4 validation folds x 3 cost scenarios execution units. The bound that the authorization enforces is max_total_config_units, the number of asset-configuration pairs; the fold and cost multipliers follow the inherited, unchanged fold and cost blocks.
bounds.resource_limits: the v6 execution protocol records max_logical_runs 1 and checkpoint_every_n_shards 10; the run is resumable and never retries unboundedly

benchmark.alignment_rule: the asset series and the benchmark series are sliced to the same fold window before the frozen engine is called
benchmark.alignment_methodology: docs/research_protocol.md:101 - Align BTC and target asset by UTC candle close
benchmark.methodology_rule: Align BTC and target asset by UTC candle close; no forward fill for missing BTC observations
fail_closed: the benchmark series does not cover an evaluated window of the asset series
the benchmark series carries a different timestamp than the asset series inside an evaluated window
benchmark.grid_rule: the 576 btc_ema_168 configurations per asset are evaluated, never dropped, re-derived or re-ranked
benchmark.exposure_rule: the benchmark dataset is development data; it lies entirely before every open confirmatory window and no confirmatory-window candle is read
benchmark.note: The v6 benchmark is the v6-cutoff-bounded dataset that the v6 data manifest publishes in its benchmark block. The dataset file lives under research/data/candles_v6/ in the v6 namespace. Its last candle closes exactly at the v6 development cutoff. The dataset is hash-verified before every use, it covers every evaluated validation window of the evaluated assets with identical timestamps, and the asset series and the benchmark series are sliced to the same fold window before the frozen engine is called.

effective_data_manifest.note: The effective v6 data manifest is the base manifest alone; v6 publishes no data-manifest amendment. The benchmark dataset is published by that manifest, in its benchmark block.

stopping_conditions: Normal completion within the recorded bounds
No candidate survives the unchanged v1 selection rule -> report the outcome (do not hide it)
Any boundary violation -> abort and rollback
A technical interruption -> keep the verified shards and resume the same run
authorized_run.rollback_rule: Do not write to v1, v2, v3, v4 or v5 artifacts; remove any newly created v6 artifact if the execution is aborted; do not alter research_state/checkpoint.json, research_state/checkpoint_v2.json, research_state/checkpoint_v3.json, research_state/checkpoint_v4.json, research_state/checkpoint_v5.json or the v1, v2, v3, v4 or v5 campaign state.
falsifiers: Any modification to src/breakout_research/ (would change the code hash)
Reading any candle in the v6 confirmatory window during selection
Reading any candle that closes inside the open v2, v3, v4 or v5 confirmatory window
Writing into v1, v2, v3, v4 or v5 shards, ledger, tallies or result streams
Reusing the v1 holdout, or the v2, v3, v4 or v5 confirmatory window
Reusing the v3 or v4 chain's benchmark dataset
Mixing v1, v2, v3, v4 or v5 cycle units with v6 results
Widening or narrowing the frozen candidate set
Dropping, re-deriving or re-ranking the 576 btc_ema_168 configurations
Evaluating the BTC filter on a benchmark series that does not cover an evaluated window of the asset series, or whose timestamps differ inside it
A second run attempt under this authorization

not_authorized.statement: This artifact authorizes one bounded v6 selection run and nothing else. It does not authorize a confirmatory-window evaluation, a candle fetch, a change to the hashed source set, an edit of a frozen artifact or a v1 re-authorization. The selected-configuration manifest that the v6 confirmatory window requires must be committed and hash-bound before the first confirmatory-window candle is read, and the v6 confirmatory evaluation may not start before the effective gate 2027-01-20T02:00:00Z.

v1_campaign_authorization.note: The functional field of the authorization is recorded, not the digest of its bytes: the controller refreshes the authorized_at_utc timestamp, so the file digest changes without the authorization changing.

residual_limitations.location: the v6 selection run's result volume
residual_limitations.limitation: The bounded run writes 193536 execution units. At the v1 record size this is of the order of 0.5 GB of shards and of the order of 100 MB of result stream. The v1 shards are bounded to 4 MiB per file; the v1 result stream was a single file of 50 MB that the campaign could not push as one blob.
residual_limitations.consequence: The shards under research/shards_v6 are the authoritative record set and are committed as bounded files of at most 4 MiB each, as the v1 campaign did. The single-file result stream research/results_v6.jsonl is expected to be large and is a projection of the verified shards, regenerated from them. The ledger, the results manifest and the checkpoint are small and are committed. The v1, v2, v3, v4 and v5 artifacts stay untouched either way.

residual_limitations.limitation: The v6 data manifest publishes the benchmark in its benchmark block and not in the assets map, so the manifest-driven asset loader cannot resolve it; the benchmark is read directly and verified against the published content hash and the canonical hourly-CSV content hash.
residual_limitations.consequence: The benchmark rule is still fully implemented: the dataset is hash-verified, it covers every evaluated window of each evaluated asset with identical timestamps, and both series are sliced to the same fold window before the frozen engine is called. No observation is forward-filled. The published block is inside the manifest's own self-hash, so the benchmark identity is part of the v6 data-manifest identity.

residual_limitations.limitation: src/v6_campaign does not exist yet; the authorization records v6_execution_path_exists: false and binds no path digest. When the path is created, its canonical source digest must be recorded in a revised authorization.
residual_limitations.consequence: No v6 selection run can execute until src/v6_campaign exists and its digest is recorded. Until then, this authorization is a design artifact only.

durability.note: Becomes durable when the commit that carries this artifact exists. The artifact is not rewritten after that commit, because its manifest_hash must not change.

hashing.note: manifest_hash is the sha256 of the document body with manifest_hash removed, following the pattern of the other v2, v3, v4 and v5 artifacts.
